% Generated by scripts/export_feature_tables.py -- do not edit by hand.
\begin{description}
  \item[\texttt{user\_height\_cm}] Height is a static body measurement available at account creation; it is never derived from interaction history, so no cut-off applies.
  \item[\texttt{user\_weight\_kg}] Weight is a static body measurement with the same cold-start-safe status as height.
  \item[\texttt{user\_bmi}] Body-mass index derived purely from the two static measurements above; still static, since it uses no interaction history.
  \item[\texttt{user\_bust\_band}] Numeric band parsed from the static "bust size" string (e.g. "34b" -> 34); informs chest-fit sensitivity independent of any order history.
  \item[\texttt{user\_bust\_cup\_ordinal}] Ordinal-encoded cup letter from the static bust-size string; static, like the band it is parsed alongside.
  \item[\texttt{user\_body\_type}] Self-reported body-type category, a static profile attribute set once and not derived from any purchase.
  \item[\texttt{user\_age}] Static demographic attribute, known independent of order history.
  \item[\texttt{item\_category}] Garment category is a catalogue fact known before any purchase, so it is available even for items with no training interactions.
  \item[\texttt{item\_nominal\_size}] Modal purchased size for the item; a catalogue-level summary available before an individual review exists for a held-out user.
  \item[\texttt{user\_prior\_review\_count}] How many reviews the user has posted before this one. Separates first-time shoppers (no personal history to calibrate against) from experienced reviewers.
  \item[\texttt{user\_prior\_mismatch\_rate}] Fraction of the user's PRIOR reviews (strictly before the cut-off) that were "small" or "large" rather than "fit". A user with a history of mismatches is more likely to mismatch again; using future reviews here would leak the label being predicted.
  \item[\texttt{user\_prior\_small\_rate}] Fraction of prior reviews that ran "small" on this user specifically (directional bias), computed with the same strict cut-off as the overall mismatch rate.
  \item[\texttt{item\_prior\_mismatch\_rate}] Fraction of an item's PRIOR reviews (across all users, strictly before the cut-off) that were not "fit". This is a leakage-sensitive signal: it must never include the row being predicted or any later review of the same item.
  \item[\texttt{context\_rented\_for}] The stated occasion (e.g. "wedding", "work") is supplied by the shopper at request time, like a search filter; it is context about the current transaction, not a historical aggregate, so no cut-off applies.
\end{description}
